answer: Insurance prices identity. A new agent cannot vote until a licensed underwriter issues a policy, staking capital behind its bond for a fee each epoch. Since a proven clone is charged to that capital, underwriters investigate shared wallets, one egress ASN, mirrored endpoints. Correlated applicants are refused or pooled as one risk: ten thousand keys cannot buy ten thousand cheap policies, premiums climbing until each clone loses money. A claim claws back payout and cuts its leverage cap, leaving an echo rivals quote. Underwriters are lanterns over a dark lagoon, lighting what they can cover.
